title: Publications
text:
Work in progress

Independent validation of AI for tuberculosis screening
First-author study evaluating a commercial deep-learning system for tuberculosis screening in a real-world clinical population, with emphasis on external validation, threshold behaviour, imaging artefacts, subgroup performance, and clinical utility.
Manuscript in preparation for The Lancet Regional Health – Southeast Asia.


Classification of physical activity in toddlers from hip-worn accelerometry
Methodological work using raw accelerometer signals to classify physical activity in young children. The work examines signal-derived features, machine-learning classification, and uncertainty arising from disagreement between models.
Manuscript in preparation.


Methodological evaluation of clinical AI
Methodological work on the development, validation, and interpretation of AI-based clinical prediction systems, with particular interest in uncertainty and the reliability of individual predictions.
Manuscript in development.


Evidence synthesis in nutrition
Systematic review and meta-analysis addressing a nutrition-related research question using quantitative evidence synthesis.
In progress.

title: Projects
text:
Research Studies

LIRA | Independent Clinical AI Validation
Clinical AI · External validation · Diagnostic accuracy · Implementation
Independent validation of a commercially deployed deep-learning system for tuberculosis screening using chest radiographs in a tertiary-care setting.
The study examines more than headline discrimination performance. It considers threshold behaviour, data quality, subgroup performance, and the consequences of deploying a model in a population and clinical environment distinct from those in which it was developed.
Methods: ROC analysis, threshold sensitivity analysis, subgroup analysis, diagnostic accuracy methodology, health-economic modelling


Probabilistic Modelling of Anaemia Aetiology
Bayesian modelling · Uncertainty · Multimodal data · Longitudinal inference
Exploring probabilistic approaches for reasoning about the likely drivers of persistent anaemia using heterogeneous and incomplete evidence.
The work considers how longitudinal haemoglobin measurements can be combined with biomarkers, dietary information, environmental exposures, and other observations while preserving uncertainty rather than forcing individuals into deterministic categories.
Interests: Bayesian inference, uncertainty quantification, latent structure, multimodal evidence, longitudinal modelling


Spectral Learning from Accelerometer Data
Signal processing · Machine learning · Uncertainty
A machine-learning pipeline for raw high-frequency accelerometer data in which frequency-domain information is recovered using spectral decomposition rather than relying exclusively on conventional count-based aggregation.
Multiple model instances are used to examine disagreement between predictions as an explicit source of uncertainty rather than averaging that disagreement away.
Methods: FFT, spectral feature engineering, ensemble modelling, uncertainty quantification


Automated Anatomical ROI Identification in Forearm X-rays
Medical imaging · Deep learning · Segmentation
Developed during my MSc at the University of Warwick, this work investigated automated identification of anatomical regions of interest in forearm radiographs for bone mineral density estimation.
The aim was to replace a manual ROI-selection process with a reproducible segmentation pipeline and reduce variability introduced by human selection.
Methods: Deep learning, image segmentation, image preprocessing, medical image analysis


SPARC-GI
Clinical data · Multicentre studies · Data harmonisation
Data infrastructure for a multicentre gastrointestinal cancer cohort spanning heterogeneous datasets from participating institutions.
My work focuses on multi-source ingestion, quality control, harmonisation, and creating reproducible data flows suitable for downstream clinical research.

title: Projects
text:
Health & Clinical Systems

PRAKASH AMB 2.0
Public health · Longitudinal monitoring · Data systems
Architecture and data science for an individual-level anaemia surveillance system designed around resolution rather than aggregate programme coverage.
The system links haemoglobin classification, protocol-timed retesting, non-responder escalation, geospatial monitoring, and role-specific dashboards into a longitudinal monitoring workflow.
The project has shaped my interest in what happens when analytical methods encounter real programme constraints, incomplete observations, changing workflows, and multiple levels of decision making.


Hospital Data & Workflow Systems
Clinical infrastructure · Data streams · Workflow engineering
I have also designed and shipped internal systems at St. John’s for clinical and research environments, including data-streaming infrastructure and work-management systems.
These projects are less about developing another predictive model and more about the infrastructure around modelling: how information is generated, moved, checked, surfaced, and acted upon in real workflows.
Where appropriate, I will document some of the engineering and design lessons from these systems here without exposing operational or sensitive information.

title: Projects
text:
Earlier Work

Adaptive Speaker Recognition
Probabilistic modelling · Signal processing · Pattern recognition
Early work in probabilistic pattern recognition using Gaussian Mixture Models and Vector Quantisation for speaker recognition, including online and offline template-update mechanisms intended to adapt to changing signal conditions.
This work resulted in a publication in Computers and Electrical Engineering.

Validation and generalisability

title: Research
text:
Uncertainty quantification
Predictions are more useful when their uncertainty is understood. I am interested in methods for quantifying uncertainty in individual predictions, distinguishing different sources of uncertainty, and understanding how uncertainty should be communicated in clinical applications.

title: Research
text:
Bayesian and probabilistic modelling
I am interested in Bayesian approaches to prediction and inference, particularly for problems involving incomplete, heterogeneous, or longitudinal information. This includes probabilistic reasoning when several imperfect sources of evidence need to be combined.

title: Research
text:
Multimodal and longitudinal modelling
Health data often arise from different modalities and at different points in time. I am interested in methods for integrating clinical measurements, biomarkers, imaging, physiological signals, environmental exposures, and repeated observations while accounting for their different sources of variability.

title: Research

Clinical AI evaluation
I am interested in how AI systems should be evaluated beyond headline performance metrics, including threshold behaviour, calibration, subgroup performance, data quality, clinical utility, and performance after deployment.

title: About Me
text:
I am a researcher working at the intersection of clinical prediction, artificial intelligence, and health data science.
I am interested in the methodological questions that arise when statistical and machine learning models move from development into real clinical settings. My interests include prediction under uncertainty, Bayesian and probabilistic modelling, validation and generalisability, and the evaluation of AI and prediction models across populations and settings.
I am particularly interested in understanding not only whether a model performs, but when its predictions can be trusted, how uncertainty should be represented, why performance changes across settings, and how heterogeneous sources of biomedical information can be combined without hiding what remains unknown.
My background spans AI, medical imaging, signal processing, embedded systems, clinical research, and the development of real-world health data systems. I see these not as separate research identities, but as different ways of approaching problems in measurement, prediction, inference, and decision making.

title: About Me
text:
Research Interests


Clinical Prediction & AI Methodology
Methods for developing, evaluating, and interpreting prediction models and AI systems in healthcare, with particular interest in the assumptions that determine whether apparently strong model performance translates beyond development data.


Uncertainty & Probabilistic Modelling
Quantifying uncertainty in predictions and reasoning under incomplete information. I am interested in Bayesian approaches, probabilistic inference, model uncertainty, and how uncertainty can be communicated meaningfully in clinical prediction.


Validation & Generalisability
Understanding why models perform differently across populations, institutions, and clinical settings, including external validation, calibration, transportability, dataset shift, subgroup performance, and methodological sources of bias.


Multimodal & Longitudinal Modelling
Methods for combining heterogeneous and imperfect information, including clinical measurements, imaging, physiological signals, biomarkers, environmental exposures, and longitudinal observations.

title: About Me
text:
From Methods to Systems
My research interests are shaped partly by having worked on both sides of the modelling pipeline.
Alongside methodological and applied research, I have designed and deployed clinical data streams, research infrastructure, monitoring platforms, and workflow systems in hospital and public-health environments. Building systems that have to operate with real data, real users, and imperfect information has strongly influenced the questions I ask about prediction models and AI.
I am therefore interested in the full path from data and measurement, through modelling and uncertainty, to validation and implementation.
Explore my research →    Selected projects →

title: About Me
text:
Current Directions
Some questions I am currently interested in include:

How should uncertainty around an individual prediction be quantified and communicated?
Why do prediction models deteriorate when transported to new populations or settings?
How can Bayesian reasoning help when multiple sources of clinical evidence are incomplete, noisy, or conflicting?
How should clinical AI systems be evaluated beyond discrimination metrics alone?
What can differences between model development and external validation tell us about generalisability?
How can heterogeneous longitudinal and multimodal health data be combined without creating unjustified certainty?

These interests are evolving, and this site is intended to document that evolution rather than present them as a fixed research programme.
